sources.organization: National Park Service / Death Valley National Park
sources.title: Russian earthquake causes minor disturbance in Devils Hole
sources.locator: Extracted body lines38–42 and monitoring-image captions47–58
sources.text: NPS reports July 29, 2025; magnitude 8.8 offshore Kamchatka; nearly 4,000 miles; 21 minutes until waves at Devils Hole. Ten-inch waves removed some material from the shallow shelf. Biologists were less concerned than after earlier disturbances. The shelf supports most feeding and spawning; monitoring captions describe some algae and invertebrate removal.
sources.quality: Direct site-operator event report and biological interpretation. Authoritative for local observations, not an independent analysis of raw monitoring data.
limits: Distance, delay and wave size are reported NPS values. Amplitude convention and raw onset series are absent; no universal seismic speed is derived.
December/February ecological effects and the March count of 38 fish are separate observations and unused.
The before image bears July 14, 2025; the after image July 30. They are not immediately adjacent observations or a quantitative mortality comparison.

sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey / Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.title: Seismic Seiches
sources.text: Passing seismic waves can excite standing waves in enclosed water. Distant seismic seiches are associated with seismic surface waves. Seiches differ from tsunami generation by sudden sea-floor displacement; local and geological factors affect responses.
sources.quality: Established mechanism from the relevant scientific agency. A different institution from NPS, not independent replication of July 2025 cave monitoring.
limits: General physics, not a calculated Devils Hole normal mode, calibrated amplitude or exact propagation path.
No one-path model or claim that distance alone determines local wave height.

sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey / Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.title: Cool Earthquake Facts
sources.locator: Extracted body lines73–75; seiche definition and pronunciation
sources.text: USGS describes a seismic seiche as water sloshing because the ground shakes. Oscillation can persist after forcing. Pronunciation: SAYSH. Seiches can have other causes; earthquake magnitude differs from local shaking intensity.
sources.quality: Relevant official explanation for qualitative ground-water coupling and pronunciation. Only the bounded passage is used; volatile facts elsewhere on the page are unused.
limits: The shaken bathtub is a labeled analogy, not a measured simulation of cave displacement or frequency.
Magnitude does not imply identical shaking in Russia and Nevada.

sources.organization: National Park Service / Death Valley National Park
sources.title: Devils Hole
sources.text: Devils Hole is a Nevada water-filled cavern and the natural habitat of its endangered pupfish. A near-surface shelf supports foraging and spawning. Distant earthquakes have caused sloshing; the operator uses a bathtub comparison.
sources.quality: Site-operator ecological and geographic context. Related to the event report, not counted as independent replication.
limits: Older temperature, population and isolation-age wording is unused. Generic two-metre waves do not describe July 2025.
An unmapped bottom does not mean bottomless. Full cave geometry is unknown; show only an illustrative near-surface cutaway.

definitions: NPS reports that the July 29, 2025 Kamchatka earthquake caused waves in Devils Hole, a water-filled cave in Nevada.
July 29 is the Nevada/UTC calendar date. July 30 in Kamchatka is the same event on a different local calendar.
The reviewed USGS event magnitude is 8.8.
Magnitude is dimensionless, not local intensity or an asserted Richter-scale measurement.
NPS reports the Devils Hole disturbance nearly 4,000 miles from the earthquake.
Approximate reported separation; no precise geodesic distance or actual travel path implied.
NPS reports waves triggered at Devils Hole 21 minutes after the earthquake.
Reported elapsed time, not a precise onset/arrival series or universal travel-time law.
Seismic waves can travel through and along Earth; passing ground motion can set enclosed water oscillating back and forth.
Qualitative coupling; distant seiches are associated with surface waves. No exact resonance, perceptible local shaking or uniform global motion claimed.
A seismic seiche is oscillation of water already in an enclosed pool in response to seismic motion, not ocean water traveling into Nevada.
Distinguish energy transport from bulk water transport. No underground channel to Russia.
A seismic seiche is distinct from an ocean tsunami generated by displacement of seawater.
No claim that seiches are always small, tsunamis are caused only by earthquakes, or this quake generated no real ocean tsunami.
NPS reports ten-inch waves at Devils Hole for the July 2025 event.
Narrate about ten inches. Crest-to-trough, amplitude and runup conventions are not supplied; animation is not calibrated to this reported value.
The endangered Devils Hole pupfish depend on a shallow shelf near the surface for most of their food and spawning.
Shelf function, not a claim that all fish remain on it or deep water is uninhabited.
The July 2025 waves removed some material from the shelf. NPS described the disturbance as minor and biologists were less concerned than after earlier quakes.
No near-extinction, mortality count, quantified egg loss, complete food loss or confirmed population rebound.
The July 2025 waves reached two metres.
A generic older maximum cannot be transferred to this event; excluded.
The July 2025 quake almost wiped out the remaining pupfish.
Unsupported and contrary to the scoped minor impact; excluded.
A specific cave resonance period amplified the Kamchatka waves by a known factor.
No local normal-mode or forcing measurements acquired; unresolved and unselected.
Only 38 Devils Hole pupfish remain today.
The March 2025 historical count is not a current count; excluded.
Unmapped is not infinite depth; excluded.
The ocean tsunami traveled into Devils Hole.
lines: An earthquake nearly four thousand miles away made waves in this Nevada desert pool.
On July twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-five, a magnitude eight point eight quake struck off Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula.
Twenty-one minutes later, water in Devils Hole began sloshing.
But seawater hadn’t crossed the ocean into Nevada.
Seismic waves traveled through the ground.
As the ground moved, water already inside the cave rocked back and forth—like water in a shaken bathtub.
That oscillation is called a seismic seiche, different from an ocean tsunami.
The waves here were about ten inches.
Small, but enough to disturb a shallow shelf where the endangered Devils Hole pupfish feed and spawn.
This event removed some material from the shelf. The park described it as a minor disturbance.
An isolated-looking pool can reveal just how connected the ground beneath us really is.
objectives: Immediate local water motion linked to a distant earthquake. Dry rock and a narrow pool fill the main field; a simple geographic locator shows the remote origin.
Brief date, place and magnitude context. Keep the Nevada pool connected to the offshore Kamchatka origin; avoid a disaster montage or numerical overload.
Compare earthquake and reported cave response with a compressed 21-minute interval. Not real-time footage or a fabricated monitoring trace.
Make existing water identity explicit. No water stream crossing the ocean into Nevada.
Show qualitative seismic energy through and along solid Earth. No core-crossing chord or universal fixed route.
A near-surface cave cutaway separates ground/wall motion from water rocking. Label exaggerated ground motion and schematic geometry; briefly use the bathtub analogy only if it clarifies coupling.
Name the demonstrated oscillation after the causal action. Distinguish it from displaced ocean water without depicting an ocean tsunami arriving at the cave.
Give the modest reported ten-inch scale in text/context. Do not depict an unverified measurement convention or borrow the generic two-metre maximum.
Move toward the near-surface feeding shelf and a few representative pupfish. Limited food-material disturbance, with no fish deaths or entirely stripped shelf.
Show limited material movement and persistence of the habitat. The consulted before/after frames are July 14 and July 30; no invented adjacent observations or removal percentage.
Return to the original pool and distant-location connection. Resolve energy travel and local water response; end on understanding, without a generic CTA or cliffhanger.
